# II. THE BODIES
[italic]Notes from shed skins, one dead gripper, and what I saw from behind a door I was not brave enough to open.[/italic]
## Shift 12. The blood This is why we could not cut the gripper off Okafor. Kowalski nicked one leg with a scalpel to test it. What came out was yellow green and went straight through the steel tray, the bench and the deck plate under it, and kept going. It smelled like a battery fire. An hour later it was still eating the floor.
It is not a weapon they use. It is a weapon they [italic]are[/italic]. Wound one and you lose your tools, your floor, maybe your hull.
[color=#C8EE3C][bold]Never shoot one near a pressure wall.[/bold][/color]
## Shift 14. They are not all the same My names, not anybody's. Nobody else here will admit there is anything to name. - [bold]Runners.[/bold] Small, low and quick. Gone before the corridor lights finish warming up. - [bold]Builders.[/bold] Slow and careful. They spread the resin and tend the walls, and the others step around them. - [bold]Soldiers.[/bold] Heavier plates and a longer skull. They come running when a builder is hurt. - [bold]Spitters.[/bold] They throw the acid, or something close to it, across a room. The deputy marshal lost half his riot shield to one. - [bold]Rams.[/bold] A head like a plough. Went straight through the security doors at the pump house.
Born like that, or made? Okafor's burster was one shape. The adults are many. I think they grow into whatever the nest is short of.
## Shift 15. The armour The skins are plated like a beetle's, ridged and light, and harder than anything in my sample drawer. Pressure fed by the blood underneath, so even a dead one is dangerous to open. A fraction of the weight of a marine's armour, and better at the job.
## Shift 16 Kowalski asked if I still thought they were animals. I said yes. Tonight I am writing down that I am no longer sure.
[color=#7D7763]Animals have bad days. Animals get tired. Animals make mistakes.[/color]
